_sinkPassNote: v24 = ECONOMY SINK PASS 2026-08-21 (OWNER RULING): a committed daily player should need 8-12 WEEKS to exhaust current content, a casual ~6 months; it was ONE EVENING. THE LEVER IS THE SINKS, NOT THE FAUCET -- harvest stays exactly 5 per 5 seconds (EchoBonusCalculator CommonResourcePerHour 3600) because " 5 wood every 5 seconds" is legible and a player can feel it; nudging it to 3.7/tick buys nothing and costs comprehension. Scaling factors: build x4, upgrade->L2 x10, upgrade->L3 x14. The THREE STORAGE ROWS (lumberyard/foundry/silo) use their own DECREASING ladder (x16/x16/x10/x8/x6.5/x6) because a uniform multiplier on a ladder that already doubles per step walks the cost off the end of the cap ladder it is gated behind -- foundry and silo wood steps were then lowered again by hand to 2000/2700/4000/6800/12000 because they are paid in WOOD, capped by the LUMBERYARD, and must fit the MATCHED container level. HARD CONSTRAINT, pinned by DeNelle.Editor.Regression.EconomySinkCapRegression [sink-cap]: NO COST MAY EXCEED THE MAX BANKABLE AMOUNT OF THAT RESOURCE (base 2000 + one container at level 1..6 = 3k/4k/6k/10k/18k/34k). A 3000-wood cost under a 2000 cap is UNCOMPLETABLE and nothing in the game explains why. CRYSTALS AND COINS ARE UNCAPPED BY DESIGN (TownBankCapacity.UncappableResources) -- that is why the crystal-priced magical ladders run to five figures. Cost baskets are UNCHANGED in shape: scaling never moves a resource across the WO-947 regular/magical line. NOTE the knock-on: BuildTimerConfig.TierForCost derives build TIME from the authored basket, so this pass also lifts the time ladder -- which is the intended coupling (see that file: "the whole ladder re-tunes itself for free when the JSON cost pass lands").
_costBasketRule: WO-947 — OWNER ECONOMY RULING 2026-08-10, BINDING, and the four classification pins ANSWERED by the owner 2026-08-14: cost baskets separate by the structure's NATURE. REGULAR structures cost wood + iron (± food where already used) and NEVER crystals. MAGICAL / ETHEREAL structures are CRYSTALS + IRON (owner 2026-08-14 pin 1 verbatim: "Crystals and Iron") — never wood. INVARIANT: no row's build cost or upgrade step ever contains wood AND iron AND crystals together. Enforced headlessly by DeNelle.Editor.Regression.CostBasketSeparationRegression [cost-basket] — any NEW row that violates the invariant FAILS the gate. FULLY APPLIED as of v18: v17 converted 'tower_siege_tower'; v18 converts the five rows that were waiting on the pins — MAGICAL (crystals + iron, wood folded 1:1 into CRYSTALS so basket totals are unchanged): 'tower_arcane_spire', 'healing_caravan' (pin 2 verbatim: "yes AoE healing" — healing IS magical); REGULAR (crystals folded 1:1 into IRON, totals unchanged): 'jeweler' (pin 3 verbatim: "Crafting (can enbue preciouus sstones future release)" — crafting, therefore regular today; a FUTURE release may let it imbue precious stones, which would be a RE-classification then, not now) and 'tower_wall_wizard' (pin 4 verbatim: "thats a baliista mechanical" — the DATA reading wins over the id; displayName 'Ballista', element None, projectileStyle 'bolt' per the owner rename ruling 2026-07-08). The regression's pending-pin exemption list is now EMPTY. (v18 populated MagicalIds; v19 added 'arcane-tower'; v20 removed the retired Healer Tower row -- see the retirement note at the end.) THE LAST PIN IS SPENT (OWNER 2026-08-14, verbatim: "cathedral of magic is where all magic upgrades anre and can unlock new teirs of spells"): 'arcane-tower' ('Cathedral of Magic') is MAGICAL. v19 converts it — wood:60 folded 1:1 into CRYSTALS, so the basket is crystals:60 + iron:60 and the total (120) is unchanged, the same discipline used for the three v18 magical rows. This OVERRIDES the earlier agent reading that called it REGULAR by the jeweler analogy ("a shop that DEALS IN magic is still a shop"), which cited behaviorId 'GameplayBuilding' and the row's _heightNote ("despite the id this is not a tower — it is the town's one civic landmark"). THE OWNER'S DISTINCTION, recorded so nobody re-litigates it: the jeweler SELLS things that happen to be precious; the Cathedral is WHERE MAGIC UPGRADES LIVE AND WHERE NEW SPELL TIERS UNLOCK — it is the ENGINE of magical progression, not a vendor that deals in it. 'behaviorId: GameplayBuilding' describes its BEHAVIOUR (it is not a firing tower), NOT its cost class. The surface evidence genuinely points both ways, so the ruling is the tiebreak — do not re-classify it off the id, the behaviorId or the _heightNote. WO-947 IS NOW FULLY APPLIED: every classification question is closed, the regression's pending-pin exemption list is EMPTY and stays empty. v20 RETIRES the never-buildable Healer Tower row entirely (WO-990, OWNER RULING 2026-08-14, verbatim: "i do not know what the town healer is" -> "retire"). She did not recognise it because it appeared in NO build category in build-categories.json, so no player could ever build it and it had no early-economy consequence; the WO-947 pin-2 conversion had been applied to a dead row. Its BEHAVIOUR is deliberately KEPT (StructureFactory case "HealerTower") as the WO-891 support-FIELD pattern reference; 'healing_caravan' is the row's design successor and inherits the concept. Do not resurrect the row. MagicalIds therefore holds THREE ids at v20: 'tower_arcane_spire', 'healing_caravan', 'arcane-tower'.
_displayOrder: WO-963 (owner ask 2026-08-10, F8 seq 2302, verbatim: 'Can we order the carousel in order of how the tutorial presents them?'). 'displayOrder' is an OPTIONAL per-entry integer that sorts the build palette carousel. LOWER FIRST; ABSENT / 0 = UNAUTHORED and sorts AFTER every authored row, keeping its current relative position (the sort is STABLE on the catalog's row order, so an unauthored row never jumps). The palette is the only consumer (BuildPaletteVM.SortForDisplay); it changes NO gating, no group split and no cost. SEEDED TO THE TEACHING ORDER: 10 collector_lumbermill (tutorial step order 20, 'Place your Lumbermill'), 20 workshop (contextual nudge 1050, the weapons roof), 30 forge/'Armorer' (contextual nudge 1060). Gaps of 10 are deliberate so the owner can slot a row between two without renumbering. NO TOWER ROW IS AUTHORED ON PURPOSE: the tutorial's defense beat (step order 30) names a TAB ('build.tab_defenses'), not a tower id, and tower_ground_archer is already the first Tower row in this file, so the Defense group teaches the archer tower first with no key. It also keeps the three CatalogBootstrap.RegisterFallback tower rows field-equal to their catalog rows (BuildEconomyRegression gate 12 [fallback-parity] deep-compares EVERY public CatalogEntry/RepoProps field, so authoring a tower here would demand a mirrored edit there). The tutorial is NEVER read at runtime by the palette - the catalog carries the order and BuildCarouselTutorialOrderRegression is what keeps the two agreeing.
_heightCadence: OWNER RULING 2026-08-05 (verbatim): 'take whatever the y height that we use across the board, we're gonna take that as y and make this maybe one point five or one point two higher. It's only gonna be half as wide as the diameter of any of the houses. I want all of the other structures to stay within that cadence. I want all of them to be relatively the same size. Wide heights, all of that should be similar. Doesn't have to be exact, but it must be similar, all scaled to the same point.' ONE FAMILY, NOT ONE NUMBER. The dial is repo.heightMul against StructureFactory.YHeightVariable (4 m base). The fit is a UNIFORM scale, so heightMul moves HEIGHT AND FOOTPRINT TOGETHER: BuildModeController claims grid cells from StructureFactory.MeasureUprightFootprintMetres (the height-fitted model's XZ bounds), never from placement.footprint, which is only the prefab-missing fallback. THE OLD SENTENCE HERE - 'there is no width dial and none is needed' - WAS TRUE ONLY WHILE EVERY MODEL'S FITTED POSE WAS ROUGHLY BUILDING-SHAPED, and it is retired as of 2026-08-20. Fit-to-height is a single-axis promise: the scale is target / boundsY, so a model whose fitted pose is FLAT divides by a tiny number and takes its footprint along for the ride. There is now exactly ONE width dial, repo.maxFootprint, and it is a CEILING in metres on the fitted model's widest horizontal extent - it only ever scales DOWN, only ever uniformly, and it DEFAULTS TO 0 = DISARMED, so it changes nothing on any row that does not author it. Exactly ONE row authors it today (collector_farm 5.6); it is not a second cadence and never a place to hand-tune a building that height already handles. GROUPS: (1) BUILDING BASE 1.0 = 4.0 m: houses, production, vendors, storage containers, collectors, civic. This is the WIDTH REFERENCE the ruling measures against; House_Medieval_Medium fits to 5.562 m across = a 2x2 claim at the 3 m cell. (2) TOWER 1.2 = 4.8 m: reads 20 percent taller than a house and 2.778 m across = 49.9 percent of a house diameter, exactly the ruling's 'half as wide', and a 1x1 claim. 1.2 is the OWNER-RULED anchor from commit 0ac59581 (archer tower); on 2026-08-05 the rest of the tower class came off the old WO-764 1.25 onto it, so no tower is an outlier against the anchor any more. (3) SIEGE ENGINE 0.75 = 3.0 m: tower_catapult and tower_siege_tower. Machines, not architecture, so they sit deliberately UNDER the house line and read as equipment; it also keeps the wall-walk Sky Ballista from out-topping the towers once stacked on a wall. (4) LANDMARK 1.25 = 5.0 m: arcane-tower (Cathedral of Magic) ONLY. The single apex of the town, which the ruling's 'relatively the same size, doesn't have to be exact' allows for one building. (5) DECORATION, well under the family: deco_torch 0.35 = 1.4 m. EXCEPTION, NOT A CADENCE VALUE: collector_farm 1.4, AND IT IS NOW CAPPED ON THE OTHER AXIS (repo.maxFootprint 5.6). The 'do NOT normalize it to 1.0' half stands - that re-ships the shrunk farm the owner reported in commit 31b41d19. The half this key MISSED, and the owner felt it on 2026-08-20 ('farm seems to be much larger than anything else'), is that heightMul is a uniform scale and therefore a FOOTPRINT dial as well: Structures/farm measures 0.977 x 1.000 x 0.391 m natively and its (-90,0,0) euler stands the 0.391 axis up, so the 5.6 m height target came out as scale 14.34 and a 14.00 x 14.34 m footprint against a 2.8-5.8 m family (measured, logs/device/2026-08-20-portal.log). BOTH directions on heightMul are wrong for that - down re-shrinks the building, up widens it further - so the fix is the footprint ceiling, which lands the row back on the 5.47 x 2.19 x 5.60 m it rendered before the PRE-fit-euler change of 2026-08-19. The row's own _heightNote carries the full derivation. NOTE THE MECHANISM CORRECTION: the 'spindly silhouette / windmill blades inflate its Y bounds' explanation that used to sit here is not what the geometry says - the art is a flat square plot - but the number it defended was right for the pipeline of its day. DELIBERATELY LEFT UNAUTHORED: wall_wood, wall_stone and gate_stone stay on the 1.0 base. See their per-row _heightNote - lowering a wall narrows it by the same factor and opens pathable GAPS in already-saved wall runs, which is a save-compat break rather than a visual tweak. TIERS 2 AND 3 NEED NO KEYS: ReskinForLevel re-fits every tier model through the same OptsFor/EffectiveVisualHeight call, so an upgrade inherits its row's heightMul automatically; there are no per-level height fields anywhere in RepoProps.
notes: Build-mode structure catalog — DATA-DRIVEN. Add a row here (+ keep the Resources/Data/Canonical copy byte-equal) and it flows into CatalogRegistry at startup via CatalogBootstrap. 'type' / 'mustSitOn' / 'navSurface' / 'element' are enum NAMES (StringEnumConverter). 'visualPrefabPath' is a Resources-relative path (LogWarning-safe on miss per CLAUDE.md §4). 'behaviorId' is resolved to a Village component by StructureFactory.AttachBehavior — only DefenseTower / WallSegment / CrystalMine / Gate are wired; null = inert decoration. S4: 'repo.cost' is the multi-resource build cost (wood/food/iron/crystals); it is charged + refunded through the persisted ResourceLedger (EconomyService). When 'cost' is omitted / all-zero, placement falls back to charging 'buildCost' Crystals (back-compat). S5 (the CoC upgrade sink): 'repo.maxLevel' (default 1 = not upgradeable; ceiling = RepoProps.MaxStructureLevel, raised 3 -> 6 by WO-966 for the storage containers; the StructureTierVisual accent ladder still tops out at 3, which is cosmetic only) is the highest level the UPGRADE verb can reach; 'repo.upgradeCost' is an optional per-step multi-resource table indexed by the level being upgraded TO minus 2 (entry [0] = L1->L2, [1] = L2->L3, ... [4] = L5->L6). When 'upgradeCost' is omitted, the upgrade cost falls back to the build 'cost' scaled by the level being left (L1->L2 = 1x, L2->L3 = 2x) -- a fallback that goes badly wrong on a long ladder, which is why the six-level containers author the table explicitly. StructureTierVisual steps the look (scale + bronze/silver/gold accent); DefenseTower range/damage and WallSegment toughness step the stats. v5 (StructureSingleton v2, owner only-ever-one ruling): 'repo.bakedTwins' lists the legacy baked scene-root GameObject names that REPRESENT a singleton row (twin standdown/resurface + IsBuilt, enforced generically by StructureSingleton with zero per-row code); null/absent = none; only meaningful with 'repo.singleton': true.

repo._preservePrefabRotationNote: WO-928 defect A, 2026-08-08 (owner: the L3 Archer Tower is lying on its side). THE ONLY ROW IN THE CATALOG THAT CARRIES THIS FLAG. It tells StructureFactory.OptsFor to leave VisualFactory's DEF-232 identity reset OFF for this row, so the model keeps its own authored root rotation. It is correct under BOTH ways this row's art can resolve, which is exactly why it is safe to author. (1) Resources/Structures holds BOTH Tower_Wooden_Watchtower[_L2/_L3].fbx AND the same-stem .prefab, so Resources.Load('Structures/Tower_Wooden_Watchtower_L3') is AMBIGUOUS. The captured trace 'after instantiate (prefab-native pose): euler=(270.00, 0.00, 0.00)' proves the FBX is what actually loaded on the owner's machine - every wrapper prefab root in that folder is identity in the YAML, so a 270 can only have come from the FBX - and for that FBX the native 270 IS the X -90 upright correction the owner measured in Offset Forge. Preserving it stands the tower up BEFORE VisualFactory.Fit measures, which also retires the 8.34x over-scale (Fit had been measuring the SHORT axis to reach 4.8 m). (2) If the WRAPPER prefab resolves instead, this flag is a proven NO-OP: DeNelle.Editor.WoodenWatchtowerBuilder deliberately bakes the -90 onto the MODEL CHILD and leaves the root at identity, precisely because Skin stomps the root - and identity preserved equals identity reset. INELIGIBLE EVERYWHERE ELSE: the thirteen rows carrying a manual (-90,0,0) orientation are stood up by StructureFactory.Create APPLYING that -90 on top of an identity-reset root; preserve their native 270 as well and the two compose to 180 - upside down, not merely sideways. Setting the same flag on SkinOptions.Structure for the whole structure CLASS was tried and reverted the same day; see the stop block there. VERIFY ONLY ON A RETURN-TO-TOWN PASS (exit to a dungeon and come back) - a first town load seats buildings from the bake/injector path and never reaches this code, which is why the class-wide flip shipped unnoticed.
repo._upgradeTextureNote: WO-928 defect B, 2026-08-08 (owner: "that tower is now the right way, but the color is wrong"). L3 was authored with upgradeVisualPath and NO upgradeTexturePath, so StructureFactory.TexturePathForLevel returned null, the tier reskin added a FRESH TripoMaterialFixer with no forced albedo, and L3 rendered a scraped material (wooden_watchtower_3d_model_basecolor) instead of its own. This is the WO-719 mechanism and tower_arcane_spire already uses it verbatim (ArcaneSpire_2_Albedo / _3_Albedo). L2 is DELIBERATELY EMPTY: it is a NINE-PART Tripo export with a basecolor per part, and one forced albedo cannot represent nine - flattening it would trade a wrong colour for a wrong model. L2 therefore falls through to visualTexturePath, which stays null, i.e. unchanged behaviour. Only L3 moves.

orientation.note: INTENTIONALLY ZERO, AND LOCKED. manual:true at (0,0,0) follows the tower_arcane_spire precedent: it marks the row human-verified so no tool re-bakes an advisory euler here, because one WOULD double-apply on top of the correction that already lives in the prefabs. The owner measured all three wooden-watchtower models in Offset Forge on 2026-08-06 and all three need X -90; that -90 is BAKED INTO EACH PREFAB (on the model child) by DeNelle.Editor.WoodenWatchtowerBuilder, NOT applied from here. DO NOT COPY THE -90 INTO THIS ROW - two reasons, both read at source. (1) ReskinForLevel deliberately does not apply entry.orientation ('Tier models rely on their prefab-native orientation'), so this block can only ever reach the BASE visual - L2 and L3 would stay on their sides. (2) This block is applied AFTER the fit, not before: VisualFactory.Skin fits to height internally, then Create applies the orientation and only ReseatCorrectedBottom follows, which translates in Y and never re-fits. On a lying-down model the fit therefore measures the SHORT axis - L2 reads 0.519 instead of 1.000, so scale becomes 4.8/0.519 = 9.25x instead of 4.80x and the later rotation stands up a 9.25 m tower, 1.93x oversized. Baking in the prefab puts the correction upstream of that measurement. CORRECTING AN EARLIER WRONG INFERENCE ON THIS ROW: it previously claimed these FBXs 'import upright on their own' because each Tripo node carries Lcl Rotation (-90,0,0). That reasoning is WRONG - all three carry identical node data yet the measured need differs from what it implies, so the import RESULT cannot be derived from the node data. Only measurement settles it; the builder now measures the as-imported aspect and refuses to bake onto an already-standing model. Facing (Y and Z) is deliberately zero: X is a defect correction, Y/Z is a preference, and which way a building faces is the player's choice at placement (owner ruling 2026-08-06 - note that after a -90 X the yaw for this family lives on Z, not Y).

orientation.note: X +90, MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL PLACEMENT PATH (WO-1157, owner F8 2026-08-24: 'the ballista builds on its side'). THE AXIS-BAKE RETIREMENT OF 2026-08-18 WAS WRONG ON THIS ROW AND ITS OWN REASONING IS WHY: it zeroed the euler because bakeAxisConversion:1 is set on the source FBX, i.e. it concluded from a FLAG that the mesh must arrive standing. The flag says the bake was REQUESTED; it does not say the mesh came back upright. DeNelle.Editor.BallistaPlacementProbe ran StructureFactory.Create on this row beside three controls and captured the numbers (Builds/ballista-probe.log): Ballista_L1.fbx native pose euler=[90,0,0] measures 1.002w x 0.549h x 0.702d, and the SAME asset forced to identity measures 1.002 x 0.702 x 0.549 - Y and Z swapped, which is the model lying on its face. VisualFactory applies DEF-232's identity reset to the clone root, so with this euler at zero the placed ballista shipped at identity: on its side, exactly as reported. THE FAMILY IS THE PROOF, not this row alone: jeweler, barracks, workshop, forge and armorer are the same Tripo import family, ALL carry bakeAxisConversion:1, ALL author euler [90,0,0], and the owner has confirmed every one of them stands correctly in town - jeweler measured native aspect 1.372 upright vs 0.619 at identity in the same run. The ballista was the one row of that family left at zero. Do NOT re-zero it, and do NOT reach for repo.preservePrefabRotation instead: that flag is what StructureOrientationOracle A1(b) accuses when a preserved root carries a tilt, and this root carries 90 degrees of it - the euler channel is the one this family uses. HISTORY: was [-90,0,0] before 2026-08-18, then [0,0,0]; the sign is +90 because that is the asset's own native pose, measured, not inferred. manual:true is kept so no auto-baker re-tips the row. The LIVE structure orientation channel is entry.orientation here, applied by StructureFactory.Create when manual==true.

entries._heightNote: 1.4 IS NOT A CADENCE OUTLIER - DO NOT NORMALIZE IT TO 1.0. That half of the original note was right and it STANDS. What it MISSED is the other axis, and that is what the owner finally felt on 2026-08-20 ('farm seems to be much larger than anything else'): heightMul is a UNIFORM scale, so it moves the FOOTPRINT by the same factor it moves the height, and this model's fitted pose is FLAT. MEASURED on device, not theorised (logs/device/2026-08-20-portal.log, [Flow:Xform] + [Flow:VisualFactory] 'skinned'): Structures/farm is natively 0.977 x 1.000 x 0.391 m, and this row's orientation euler (-90,0,0) stands the 0.391 axis UP, so Fit divided the 5.6 m target (4 m base x 1.4) by 0.391 and produced scale=(14.34) and a fitted footprint of 14.00 x 14.34 m - against a family that measures 2.8-5.8 m across. That is 3.5x, and NO value of heightMul fixes it: lowering it re-ships the shrunk farm (commit 31b41d19), raising it makes the footprint worse. THE CORRECTION IS repo.maxFootprint 5.6 (added 2026-08-20) - a footprint CEILING that scales the fitted model DOWN uniformly until its widest horizontal extent is 5.6 m, the same number as this row's placement.footprint, so the visual and the collision claim finally agree. Final rendered size 5.47 x 2.19 x 5.60 m; the grid claim shrinks 5x5 cells -> 2x2, which is overlap-safe for saved towns. WHY THE OLD MECHANISM READ WRONG, kept so nobody re-derives it: 'the windmill blades inflate this model's Y bounds' is not what the geometry says - the art is a flat square plot, not a spindly silhouette - but the old note's CONCLUSION was correct for the pipeline it was written against. Until the GROK_BRIEF change of 2026-08-19 the euler was applied AFTER the fit, so Fit measured the UNROTATED 1.000 axis, 1.4 yielded scale 5.60, and the farm rendered at exactly 5.47 x 2.19 x 5.60 - the size the owner accepted. Moving the euler PRE-fit flipped which axis Fit divides by, and only this row's art is flat enough for that to matter. The cap value is chosen to reproduce that owner-accepted size in BOTH regimes: under the old order the widest extent is 5.60 and the cap is exactly non-binding, under the current order it binds and lands on the same numbers - so this row can no longer be resized by a change to rotation ORDER. heightMul 1.4 is deliberately KEPT and is INERT while the cap binds (any heightMul above ~0.55 lands on the same capped size); it remains the documented fallback if the cap is ever disarmed. If it ever needs retuning, retune the CAP against the rendered body standing next to a forge, never against the number.

_restoreGoldNote: TIER-ONE PRODUCER RESTORE (owner ruling 2026-08-23): a DESTROYED tier-one producer is restored for GOLD ONLY, flat, dependent on nothing else. ⛔ THIS IS A NAMED EXCEPTION TO WO-753 (destroyed items never rebuild - build fresh at full cost); it is deliberate, not a contradiction, and exists because every tier-one producer is priced in the resource it PRODUCES (the armorer costs 280 iron to build the iron producer, the lumber mill 160 wood to build the wood producer). Without this the economy closes on itself: lose the building, lose the resource, cannot afford the building. Gold is UNCAPPED by design and drops from kills (3-120, median 18), so recovery is always reachable without another building. First placement stays FREE via freeBuildsUsed (save v32).
